posts.text:
Wednesday, Nov 25: Toronto's streetcars lost 868 hours to delays, across all routes.

Slowest for its length: 509 Harbourfront eastbound. A typical 2.2 km trip lost 7 min (usually 6).
Smoothest: 507 Long Branch eastbound, 12 min over 7.8 km (usually 11).

#TTC #TransitSky #DataViz

https://stuckin.to/

Wednesday's slowest spot: Southbound on York St, at Adelaide St West.
The average streetcar lost 2 min 9 s here (usually 80 s). Across 147 trips, that adds up to 5.3 hours.
posts.alt: 3D map of York St around Adelaide St West, rotated to Toronto's street grid. Delay is drawn as a coloured ridge above the track, rising where streetcars lose time; the southbound stretch at Adelaide St West is highlighted, adding up to about 2 min 9 s lost per streetcar.

shot.title: York St southbound, at Adelaide St West
shot.sub: Wednesday, Nov 25: 2 min 9 s lost per streetcar · 147 trips

posts.text:
Most short-turned, Wednesday, Nov 25: 506 Carlton. 1 in 9 trips (37) were sent back before the end of the line, most after College St at Lansdowne Ave (westbound, 20), instead of going on to High Park.

Across all routes, 4% of trips were short-turned.
posts.alt: Map of the 506 Carlton route in the waits view: a column at each stop, taller and darker where riders waited longer than scheduled, and yellow warning signs where cars were short-turned. A tooltip on the busiest spot, after College St at Lansdowne Ave, gives how many westbound cars were sent back there instead of going on to High Park.

posts.text:
Most held at a signal, Wednesday, Nov 25: westbound at Strachan Ave & Fleet St.

46% of streetcars waited 90 s or more beyond a clean approach, about a full signal cycle, despite transit priority.
About 279 streetcars came through.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Strachan Ave & Fleet St, with arrows for each direction of streetcar travel into each signal, coloured by how often streetcars were held 90 seconds or more. A tooltip for the westbound approach reads 46% held 90 s+, with a histogram of extra time through the approach.

posts.text:
Wednesday, Nov 25: at the busiest moment (4:30 pm), 143 streetcars were in service, against 150 scheduled.
Overall, 97% of scheduled streetcar service ran, and buses ran 1,260 hours on streetcar routes.
posts.alt: Line chart of streetcars in service through Wednesday, Nov 25, every 10 minutes from 4 am, against the TTC's schedule (dashed). The busiest moment was 143 streetcars at 4:30 pm, against 150 scheduled; over the day 97% of scheduled streetcar hours ran.

posts.text:
Longest extra wait at a stop, Wednesday, Nov 25: Dundas St West at Bloor St West (504 King westbound).

A car was due about every 10 min, so the average wait should have been about 5. It was 8.4: 3.6 min extra.

Turn up at random and the chance of waiting over 10 min was 28%. On schedule: 1%.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Dundas St West at Bloor St West in the waits view, a column at each stop. A tooltip for the stop reads a 8.4 minute average wait, 3.6 more than on schedule, with a 28% chance of waiting over 10 minutes against 1% on schedule, and a chart of the spread of gaps between cars.
